transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Lumina PM), Ethan Ross (Lumina Lead ML), Priya Shah (Lumina Head of Platform), Oliver Grant (Lumina Procurement)
Artifacts referenced: Deck: https://redwood.app/decks/lumina-pilot, Benchmarks spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/lumina-bench, Security pack: https://redwood.app/security/lumina

[00:00] Sofia Alvarez: hey everyone thanks for joining, i know we're tight on time so we'll go through the final results from the pilot and outline next steps. feel free to interrupt.
[00:12] Maya Patel: thanks Sofia, excited to see the numbers — been showing these to the retail ops folks.
[00:18] Daniel Kim: quick note — i'll run through the perf chart first then we can hit accuracy and cost. i pulled the numbers for the 7-day window where the traffic shape was closest to peak.
[00:30] Ethan Ross: cool, and if you can also call out the tail latency percentiles that would be great.
[00:36] Daniel Kim: yeah so p50 is 120ms, p95 is 310ms, p99 sits at about 720ms on the hosted config we used. those are for the sequence lengths avg 120 tokens; when we used the Dedicated pool with reserved 4xA100 like we simulated, p99 dropped to ~420ms. there was an occasional spike during our 9am batch window because of cross-tenant burst — we recommended the dedicated pool for predictable tail behavior.
[01:05] Maya Patel: so just to confirm, the dedicated option gave us more consistent latency even under the morning spike?
[01:09] Daniel Kim: yep. and we also showed the fallback route — if capacity gets constrained we can route to a slightly smaller quantized variant which keeps latencies low but can add a small accuracy delta.
[01:22] Priya Shah: speaking of quantized variant, how bad was the quality delta with the int8-ish profile you tested? we care a lot about the recall on product names.
[01:30] Daniel Kim: good question. for our prompts the recall drop was minimal — we measured a 2.8% drop in exact-match for SKU extraction with the aggressive quant profile. with the conservative int8-profile + per-customer KV cache tuning the drop was <1%.
[01:45] Ethan Ross: that's acceptable; <3% sounds reasonable if the latency/cost tradeoff is meaningful. can you share the prompt-template changes you used?
[01:52] Daniel Kim: yes i'll add the prompt templates to the runbook. we did a couple of prompt-engineering tricks: explicit schema enforcement, shortened context windows by moving historical context to embeddings + retrieval, and prefix caching for sessioned flows.
[02:05] Sofia Alvarez: cost numbers — we ran the hosted API baseline at approx $0.80 per 1k requests given their token profile; with batching and dedicated reserved capacity we estimated unit cost reduced to about $0.22 per 1k requests. the workbook has line items broken down per-token compute, infra amortization, and network.
[02:25] Oliver Grant: wait 0.22 per 1k is that with a 12-month reserved commit? what's our commitment level?
[02:31] Sofia Alvarez: it's modeled on a 12-month reserved capacity for the Dedicated cluster with a modest commit (~250k tokens/day average), plus the normal network egress line item. we'll include separate scenarios in the spreadsheet: 3-month pilot pricing, 12-month reserved, and on-demand hosted.
[02:45] Maya Patel: from a product perspective the quality improvements in intent classification were the big win for us — reduced manual routing by about 18% in the sample cohort. that drives pretty clear headcount savings in the contact center.
[02:57] Ethan Ross: we also ran regenerative tests for hallucination, we saw an nlp confidence calibration issue at mid-tail lengths where creative completion bled into SKU fields; Daniel's team toggled the temperature and used function calling schema to lock outputs.
[03:12] Daniel Kim: yeah we switched to deterministic sampling on fields we care about and used structured output enforcement which fixed the hallucination spots. i'll include those settings in the runbook.
[03:22] Priya Shah: on the security side — we ran the private deployment tests in our staging VPC and the Redwood Private controller seemed to respect our KMS policies. a couple of notes: we need explicit audit log retention to comply with internal policy.
[03:35] Sofia Alvarez: noted — Redwood's Private offering includes configurable audit retention; we'll provide an options matrix with SOC2 scope and supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM).
[03:45] Priya Shah: the transcriptions earlier had a small error where the agent name mapping broke in the session logs, is that going to be resolved?
[03:52] Daniel Kim: we flagged that — it's a STT mapping issue when speaker diarization overlaps. we have a patch queued; should be out in the next patch window. not critical for logs but wanted to be transparent.
[04:05] Oliver Grant: procurement question — do you support net-45 or is net-30 standard? also need insurance certificates and an executed MSA.
[04:12] Sofia Alvarez: standard is net-30 but we can discuss net-45 for enterprise contracts; we'll send the MSA template and insurance certs along with the pricing workbook.
[04:20] Maya Patel: coming back to success criteria — for Lumina to go to production we outlined: <p99 latency 500ms on peak, <2% quality delta vs baseline, and monthly unit cost under $0.25 per 1k requests. are we comfortable these are achievable?
[04:34] Daniel Kim: yes with Dedicated + conservative quant profile + KV caching we'll hit p99 ~420ms in our sims. quality delta can be kept under 2% if you adopt the structured output and embedding retrieval pattern we used. cost target of $0.25 looks achievable with the 12-month commit numbers.
[04:48] Ethan Ross: the one open engineering risk is the SAML integration flow for service accounts, Priya is tracking that — if that slips procurement may delay.
[04:57] Priya Shah: i'm on it; i've already shared our SSO metadata with Redwood but need the IdP testing plan.
[05:03] Sofia Alvarez: Daniel will send an IdP test checklist with the runbook.
[05:08] Daniel Kim: yep will do.
[05:10] Sofia Alvarez: ok let's run through the explicit next steps: i'll send the final benchmark workbook and the term sheet; Daniel will produce the one-page runbook and IdP checklist; Ethan and Priya will validate infra and SSO; Oliver will start procurement paperwork.
[05:22] Oliver Grant: sounds good. target date for procurement kickoff is week of 2026-05-25, procurement team needs the MSA and pricing to start.
[05:30] Maya Patel: for exec signoff, i'll schedule a 30-min readout the week after the numbers land.
[05:36] Sofia Alvarez: perfect. anything else?
[05:40] Ethan Ross: just a small ask — can Redwood include a short appendix on rollback/fallback behavior in the runbook? i want the ops playbook documented.
[05:46] Daniel Kim: yep we'll include rollback procedures, routing policies and automated fallback to smaller model variants.
[05:52] Sofia Alvarez: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the materials.
[05:56] Maya Patel: thanks all. bye.

End of transcript.
